SpaceX CRS-1. On May 22, 2012, SpaceX launched its Dragon cargo spacecraft aboard a Falcon 9 rocket. This mission marked something historic: Dragon became the first private spacecraft to dock with the International Space Station, delivering over 400 kilograms of supplies and equipment.

The moment was redemptive for SpaceX. The company had lost its two previous Falcon 9 flights and the Dragon demonstration missions, and the aerospace industry had been skeptical. But CRS-1 proved that private companies could achieve what previously only government space agencies could do. The mission was part of a Commercial Resupply Services contract with NASA, marking a fundamental transition of ISS logistics from government-operated to commercially operated spacecraft.

What came next was equally important. The Dragon capsule was recovered intact in the Pacific Ocean and reused for subsequent missions, pioneering the practice of capsule reusability. SpaceX has since flown over thirty CRS missions to the International Space Station, becoming the primary resupply partner. The mission demonstrated not only that commercial spaceflight was viable but that it could reduce costs and increase access to space in ways the aerospace industry was only beginning to understand.
